segments.title: Chương 164: Lên Tudou.com mà xem
segments.content:
Chapter 167: 0164 Let's Go Check Out Tudou (Bonus Chapter for Alliance Leader 'Might as Well Go Eat')

Chen Guiliang stayed at Tao Chenggang's "Bailian Network Technology Company" for five days.

The finance and legal personnel he brought were responsible for inspecting the company's specific situation, mainly looking for any debts.

As for Chen Guiliang himself, he hung out with the game development team, requesting modifications for anything he felt was not right.

And he repeatedly emphasized that they could not directly sell experience and equipment.

No matter how much money whales spent, they must still level up by doing quests or killing monsters. Although their leveling speed would be faster, they couldn't create too large a gap with ordinary players.

Only then would it seem "fair"!

Then there was the equipment, which had to either be dropped by monsters or crafted by collecting materials. Ordinary players would honestly spend time gathering materials, while paying players could use money to buy materials.

Even paying players couldn't be allowed to buy everything at will, otherwise they would max out their gear early on, which would make the whales feel that it was no longer interesting.

Some materials had to be obtained through quests or killing monsters, or purchased from ordinary players. This enhanced the interaction between the two types of players and also created a source of income for ordinary players.

A few materials had to be obtained by opening boxes and trying one's luck.

Equipment enchanting or upgrading consumed a great deal of materials, requiring considerable effort and money from paying players.

Of course, what was more important were the systems for national wars, guilds, families, rankings, PK, quests, casual gameplay, and so on.

Early July.

ByteDance invested 1.5 million yuan into Bailian Technology, acquiring 25% of its shares.

Tao Chenggang's stake was diluted to 45.98%, but he remained the largest shareholder and held veto power on the board.

If the initial operating funds for the game were insufficient, they could borrow money from ByteDance. Of course, it would accrue interest.

The reason Chen Guiliang didn't invest more was to protect the founder's equity and to leave enough room for future financing, making it easier to raise funds and go public down the line.

When Tao Chenggang first started developing the game, he had been following Chen Guiliang's idea and continuously updating a thread on 17173.com.

"March 18, 2004. Brothers and sisters, for my dream, I'm going to make a game. I've already registered Bailian Network Technology Company. I have three startup partners..."

"March 29, 2004. The game development team has been established. For now, we only have 15 people..."

"April 10, 2004. I sold one of my net cafes. The startup capital is almost gone, I have to keep pouring it in... Two more brothers have joined the development team..."

"June 21, 2004. I sold 'Abyss Legend' and two more net cafes. Making a game really is a money pit..."

"2004..."

Due to his previous "Legend Refugee Post," Tao Chenggang's account had always been followed by some netizens.

When he first posted about making a game, some people mocked him, some were skeptical, but many also encouraged him.

But as the "game development thread" was continuously updated, and as he kept selling his net cafes to raise funds, the tone of the replies gradually changed. There were still people who mocked him for overreaching, but there were more netizens encouraging him, and many even urged him to quit while he was ahead.

Finally, in the winter of 2004, Tao Chenggang began posting in-game screenshots.

Although they were all works in progress, they proved to the netizens that he was, indeed, making a game.

"Brother Yijian Xilai, can you give me your bank account number? Even though my salary isn't high, I can still support you with a few dozen yuan."

"No need. I'm making this game for my dream."

"The OP is completely insane. I counted, you've already sold five net cafes. How many do you have left to sell?"

"I still have three net cafes."

"I'm impressed."

"I'll definitely check it out when the game is done!"

"I advise the OP to quit while you still can. Online games aren't something you can handle."

After that, Tao Chenggang increased the frequency of his posts, popping up almost every one or two days.

And most of it had nothing to do with the game.

For example: "There was another power outage today. This science park was just completed, and there's still a lot of construction going on around here. The power gets cut for an hour or two from time to time."

And another: "A brother from the development team left. I wish him a bright future."

More and more netizens started following the "game development thread." Anyone who frequently browsed 17173.com more or less knew that someone was selling everything they owned to make a game.

Until one day, Tao Chenggang posted again: "Brothers and sisters, I've sold all my net cafes. Haha, the next step is to sell my house..."

"Holy crap! I just got back after being abroad for half a year, and you're still making this game?"

"I'm so freaking moved, I'm crying. For real."

"Brothers, I am witnessing a dream chaser."

"I'll bet fifty cents that the OP will definitely lose his entire fortune."

A while ago, Tao Chenggang posted again: "I'm very happy today. Two more friends have become shareholders. They invested a total of 400,000 yuan..."

"Congratulations, OP."

"Two more suckers have fallen into the pit."

"If the game flops, the OP isn't going to jump off a building, is he?"

"Here to cheer on Yijian Xilai."

Now, Tao Chenggang posted once more: "July 3, 2005. I have good news to announce today. ByteDance has invested 1.5 million yuan in my company. The game will be ready for closed beta in 60 days at the most. We are now collecting name suggestions for the game. The background of this game is... The netizen whose game name is selected will automatically receive closed beta access to this game, and I will also send a small gift..."

"Which company is ByteDance? Are they that desperate?"

"Dude upstairs, you don't know about Xiaonei?"

"I've heard of Xiaonei. It was pretty popular last month. The 19-year-old multi-millionaire, right?"

"ByteDance is the parent company of Xiaonei."

"Haha, a 19-year-old company boss investing in a blockhead who's selling everything to make a game. That's a match made in heaven."

"I read the game's story background. How about 'Tyrannical Reign Over the World' (Wangba Tianxia)?"

"Goddamn 'Turtle Over the World' (Wangba Tianxia)."

"I suggest calling it 'Divine Martial Storm' (Shenwu Fengyun)."

There were still plenty of jokes, but more and more people were helping to come up with a name for the game.

This created such a sense of participation; even the game's name was being chosen by the netizens themselves!

When the game truly launched, there would probably be a lot of organic publicity from fans.

Chen Guiliang scanned the thread for a while, then said to Tao Chenggang, "You can set up an official game website now. Keep posting on 17173 to drive traffic to the official site. Continuously update the game information on the website, and list the candidate game names for netizens to vote on."

"That's what I was thinking too," Tao Chenggang said with a smile.

Chen Guiliang continued to offer ideas, "After the game is launched, use the official website's traffic and voting data for promotion. On one hand, run ads on other websites, and on the other, use this data to negotiate partnerships with net cafes. If the data doesn't look good, then make it look good. Also, you can contact that editor from 'Popular Software' again. This kind of story is novel enough that he'd most likely be willing to report on it for free."

Tao Chenggang said, "I've kept in touch with that editor. He often encourages me."

"That's even better."

Chen Guiliang left Hangzhou and headed straight for Shanghai.

He wasn't going to attend the "Mengya" writers' forum, but to meet with Wang Wei of Tudou.

ByteDance's business empire needed to be pieced together bit by bit, and investing now required very little capital.

Tudou's domain name was registered four months earlier than YouTube's.

But development didn't start immediately, causing its launch to be one month later than YouTube's.

Wang Wei's previous position was Executive President of Bertelsmann Online China.

At the beginning of this year, he took out his 1 million yuan in savings, gathered four partners, and rented a three-bedroom apartment in Shanghai as their office.

One day in early July, Wang Wei was eating instant noodles.

They were too lazy to go downstairs, so they ate this stuff often.

Tao Pei, who was in charge of business affairs, picked up the landline, "Hello, this is Tudou... It's not a cold call? ByteDance wants to inve... Hold on!"

Tao Pei rushed over to Wang Wei in a few steps. "ByteDance wants to invest in us."

Wang Wei swallowed the instant noodles in his mouth, and wearing a pair of slippers, he slowly walked over to take the call. "Hello, I'm the founder of Tudou... Okay, I'm free anytime... My address is..."

After hanging up, Wang Wei found that all his partners were looking at him.

Wang Wei smiled. "ByteDance said they want to invest. They'll fly over to meet in a couple of days."

"Yeah!"

Everyone cheered.

They were feeling very lost at the moment.

All of Tudou's funding was Wang Wei's 1 million yuan in savings.

In the two-plus months since it went online, user growth was average, but the money was burning faster and faster, and they had only secured two or three small ad deals.

In another six months, Wang Wei's 1 million yuan in startup capital would be just about gone.

Then IDG would come along to invest, taking a 33.33% stake in Tudou for 500,000 USD. This would lead to Tudou's equity structure becoming extremely complicated after its Series B financing!

But Wang Wei had no choice at the time. Otherwise, Tudou would have had to shut down early.

But in this timeline, Chen Guiliang had arrived early.

"Boss, shouldn't you do something about your appearance?" one of his partners reminded him.

Wang Wei said, "It's fine. It's all the same."

This guy was a slipper-wearing champion. When he met the investors from IDG, he had also just worn slippers.

Now meeting Chen Guiliang, he was wearing slippers as well.

"Hello, I'm at the entrance to the residential complex."

"Which gate?"

"The main gate."

"Wait a moment, I'll be right there."

Chen Guiliang handed out cigarettes and chatted with the complex's security guard. He waited for a good ten-plus minutes before seeing a young man approach.

A buzz cut, T-shirt, shorts, and slippers. His hands were empty, looking like an unemployed youth who had just stepped out to buy cigarettes.

The only thing he didn't look like was a founder coming to discuss financing.

Chen Guiliang quite liked his film "White Snake," but "Chang'an San Wan Li" was a bit of a chaotic adaptation.

"New Gods: Yang Jian" was even less impressive.

However, the name of Wang Wei's company was exceptionally good: Light Chaser Animation.

Chen Guiliang liked people who were willing to chase the light.

"Hello, Mr. Wang," Chen Guiliang waved.

Wang Wei smiled and walked over to shake his hand. "I don't deserve to be called Mr. Wang. I just made a small website. Mr. Chen, why don't you come and take a look at my place first."

Chen Guiliang followed him into the residential complex, took the elevator upstairs, and arrived at the three-bedroom apartment.

The inside had been tidied up a bit; at least it didn't smell like instant noodles anymore.

Wang Wei's four partners were all standing in the living room to welcome them.

They were all young people, and they were quite excited to see Chen Guiliang. Someone even regarded Chen Guiliang as a startup idol.

"It's a bit simple. Please, have a seat on the sofa," Wang Wei said.

Chen Guiliang didn't go to the sofa. Instead, he first looked around the living room, then went to observe the bedrooms, and praised, "Not bad. It's much bigger than my office last autumn."

Wang Wei even had his own private office—his bedroom.

"Let's talk business directly," Wang Wei said, straight to the point, not wanting to waste time.

(End of this chapter)
